nodes.text: Run mass spectrometry to determine molecular weight and formula
Mass spec shows molecular ion at m/z 127.09971 (100%), M+1 at 128.10284 (8.12%)
M+1 peak of ~8% indicates ~7-8 carbons; molecular formula C7H13NO (MW ~127.10) is most likely; DBE=2 suggests 2 degrees of unsaturation

support.quote: The M+1 peak of ~8% suggests the presence of carbon atoms (each carbon contributes ~1.1% to M+1). This indicates approximately 7-8 carbons.

nodes.text: Run 1H NMR to understand the structure
All singlets with no vinyl H suggest methyl groups on quaternary/heteroatom carbons; 6H singlet suggests two equivalent methyls; one exchangeable proton (NH) likely absent from spectrum

support.quote: All signals are singlets, which suggests: No coupling between protons, Likely methyl groups attached to quaternary carbons or heteroatoms
The signal at 2.65 ppm (3H) could be N-CH3 (N-methyl group).

nodes.text: Run 13C NMR to confirm the carbon framework
Simulate spectra for CC(C)=C(C)C(=O)N(C)C to verify hypothesis
13C signals indicate one carbonyl (~161 ppm, amide), two sp2 C=C carbons (143.85 and 130.30), and four aliphatic methyls; structure likely has tetrasubstituted double bond

The absence of vinyl protons suggests the double bond is tetrasubstituted!
